item.title: Puppeteer updates installation workflow and adds WebMCP and MCP support
item.description:
Puppeteer updates installation workflow and adds WebMCP and MCP support

Puppeteer, a JavaScript library for controlling Chrome or Firefox, has updated its installation behavior to accommodate modern package manager security defaults, while expanding its capabilities with new API support and an MCP server integration.

🔍 Overview

Puppeteer provides a high-level API to control Chrome or Firefox over the DevTools Protocol or WebDriver BiDi. By default, the tool runs in headless mode, meaning no visible user interface is displayed. Recent developments include the introduction of a Puppeteer-based Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for browser automation and debugging, as well as support for the experimental WebMCP API.

⚙️ Key details

Modern package managers, including npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun, and Deno, now block dependency install scripts by default. Because Puppeteer traditionally downloaded a compatible Chrome binary during the npm i puppeteer installation step, this security feature can prevent the browser from downloading, leading to runtime errors.

To address this, developers have two main options:

  • Manually download the required browsers after installation by running the command npx puppeteer browsers install.
  • Configure the package manager to allow the specific install script to run. For example, with npm, developers can add “puppeteer” to the “allowScripts” array in the package.json file.

Alternatively, developers can use npm i puppeteer-core to install Puppeteer as a library without automatically downloading Chrome.

🧩 How it works

A standard workflow involves launching a browser instance, opening a new page, navigating to a URL, and interacting with elements using locators and keyboard actions. The library supports querying elements by CSS selectors or by accessible names, allowing for robust interaction with web content.

💡 Why it matters

The updates ensure Puppeteer remains compatible with the default security settings of contemporary package managers while expanding its utility through the installation of the chrome-devtools-mcp server. This allows for enhanced browser automation and debugging workflows.

#Puppeteer #JavaScript #BrowserAutomation #DevTools #MCP #WebDevelopment

Source: puppeteer/puppeteer

item.title: Eido 0.0.2 Adds Browser Automation and Localization to Native AI Workspace
item.description:
Eido 0.0.2 Adds Browser Automation and Localization to Native AI Workspace

Eido 0.0.2 is now available for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 13 or later. This update introduces browser and desktop automation capabilities, expanded localization options, and interface refinements for the native AI workspace built on Zed and the official pi agent.

🌐 Localization Updates

The interface now supports English and Simplified Chinese. Users can select Follow System, English, or 简体中文 at the top of the Settings menu. While common Eido controls and menus are localized, user content, code, model output, and tool identifiers remain unchanged.

🖥️ Interface Refinements

Several visual and usability improvements have been applied to the workspace:

  • Interface and conversation text default to 16px.
  • Ordinary completed tasks no longer leave a detached “Run finished” label; important status messages stay aligned with the input area.
  • Existing custom font preferences are preserved.
  • Users can drag the empty area in the top toolbar to move a non-fullscreen window on macOS.

🌐 Browser and Computer Use

The update introduces experimental features for extending tasks to websites and desktop applications. These capabilities are disabled by default and require separate DeepSeek service configuration. The release includes Chromium and its desktop driver. Users can also connect an existing Poki MCP installation to supported iPhone workflows, though Poki and device preparation are separate setup steps. Automation compatibility varies by website, application, and device.

To enable Computer Use, users must update global settings and grant specific macOS permissions:

  1. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security.
  2. Allow Eido under Accessibility and Screen & System Audio Recording (called Screen Recording on some macOS versions).
  3. Restart Eido.

These permissions allow input and window capture. Note that replacing a locally signed build can require re-enabling these permissions, and permission previously granted to a standalone Cua Driver does not apply to Eido.

🧩 Workflow and Configuration

The update retains pi’s public configuration and authentication interfaces while updating runtime adaptation. Key workflow features include:

  • Reference relevant files with @ and attach supporting material.
  • Continue earlier tasks with their saved context.
  • Review proposed file changes in the native editor before accepting them.
  • Search and fetch sources, inspect saved evidence, extract PDF/image text, and connect requirements with proposed changes and checks.

Model and thinking controls are located beside the composer in AI → pi Models & Credentials. Configuration and task history are stored outside the application bundle and are preserved during local updates.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Bundled Agent: pi 1.5.2
  • Signing Status: Locally signed; has not been notarized by Apple.
  • Release Assets: Include SHA-256 checksums, Eido source, and corresponding source for the native components.

#Eido #Zed #AIWorkspace #BrowserAutomation #macOS #PiAgent

Source: tony3liu/eido

item.title: Browser Use releases Pi Mono-based web agent with cloud browser support
item.description:
Browser Use releases Pi Mono-based web agent with cloud browser support

Browser Use has announced a new AI web agent built on Pi Mono, described as a tiny TypeScript web agent that hill climbed on real browser evaluations. The agent writes JavaScript, controls Chrome, and builds the helpers it needs dynamically. It uses Pi Mono plus a persistent V8 REPL and raw CDP to enable programmability with sessions, saved logins, streaming and typed results. The implementation is provided as a single SDK that can be integrated into applications via npm install @browser_use/pi, pnpm add @browser_use/pi, or bun add @browser_use/pi. Developers need Node 22.19+ or Bun 1.3.14+ (with Bun requiring Node for the V8 worker). The system uses Browser Use Cloud, so no local Chrome installation is needed, and supports upstream Pi’s model catalog and transports with custom providers, sessions with follow-ups and saved logins, persistent workspaces, and cloud browsers or user-owned Chrome. An ultrafast mode minimizes waits after actions, and the platform provides interaction highlights, recordings, and GIF exports. JavaScript runs in a separate worker with filesystem and network access, while anonymous run counters are enabled by default but can be disabled through telemetry settings or the DO_NOT_TRACK environment variable.

#AIagents #TypeScript #webautomation #PiMono #BrowserAutomation

Source: browser-use/browser-use-pi

item.title: Microsoft releases MagenticLite as next-gen agentic app
item.description:
Microsoft releases MagenticLite as next-gen agentic app

MagenticLite is an experimental agent that expands the capabilities of Magentic-UI by enabling cross-platform automation across the browser and local file system.

🔍 Overview

MagenticLite is the next generation of Magentic-UI, an agentic application from Microsoft AI Frontiers, redesigned to perform more tasks with fewer resources.

🧩 How it works

MagenticLite pairs two specialized models to deliver agentic performance without heavy compute:

  • MagenticBrain: An on-device-friendly orchestrator model
  • Fara: A specialized model for browser use

This design allows real work to be automated without relying on frontier-scale compute.

Workflow capabilities

  • Web research
  • Form filling
  • File management
  • All within a single workflow

User control features

  • Steer, approve, or take over at any point
  • MagenticLite stops and checks in before taking critical actions

Security features

  • Browser sessions run inside a lightweight VM sandbox named Quicksand
  • The agent cannot access the rest of your machine without explicit user permission

⚙️ Key details

Model Purpose Compute requirement
MagenticBrain Orchestrator On-device-friendly
Fara Browser automation Specialized for browser use

Supported tasks

  • Fill expense forms
  • Find prices for recipe ingredients
  • Find and book a restaurant
  • Organize local files

🚀 Availability

Installation steps

  1. Create a project directory 
    1

    mkdir magentic-lite && cd magentic-lite
  2. Create and activate a virtual environment 
    1
2

    uv venv --python=3.12 --seed .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
  3. Install the latest 0.2.x release from PyPI 
    1

    uv pip install "magentic_ui>=0.2.0"
  4. Start the application 
    1

    magentic-ui --port 8081
  5. Open the web interface
    • URL: http://127.0.0.1:8081/
    • Follow the in-app onboarding to connect a model endpoint

Legacy version

  • The previous Magentic-UI 0.1 release (optimized for frontier models) is available on the magentic-ui-0.1 branch

Platform support

  • macOS
  • Windows (with WSL)

Licensing

  • Microsoft and contributors grant a license to any code in the repository under the MIT License

💡 Why it matters

MagenticLite demonstrates that strong agentic performance can be achieved with small, efficient models, reducing reliance on large-scale compute resources while maintaining user control and safety.

#MagenticLite #AIagents #MicrosoftAI #agenticapps #browserautomation
